reasons: The cited text (9.1–9.3, 9.5) contains only for-cause, insolvency, and security/SLA termination rights, so the claimed missing Customer convenience right in a three-year term is a genuine deviation under the rule's missing-behaviour guidance.

The inserted 9.4 tracks the preferred position and model language: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice, no penalty or early-termination charge, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a term.
Placement and numbering are clean — 9.4 is inserted after 9.3 into an existing gap (original jumps from 9.3 to 9.5), so no renumbering conflict is created.
The comment accurately describes the change, cites the playbook rationale, and offers the 60-day fallback without lecturing; tone and prefix conform.

Minor, non-blocking: the cross-reference to Section 10.2 for refund mechanics is not verifiable from the supplied excerpts, but the clause states the refund obligation self-sufficiently, so the edit remains operative even if that reference needs conforming.
